newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs Tuesday were seen selling at prices steady to $0.50 per cwt lower than Monday, pressured by thin demand from packers fighting unprofitable margins, dealers and packer buyers said.
Margins were pushed deeper into unprofitable territory as wholesale pork prices generally slipped Monday and cash hogs mostly sold steady-$0.50 higher in direct trade, they noted.

Cash prices were underpinned early Monday by packers caught short of hog inventories who had to scramble to get "start-up" hogs following the three-day holiday weekend, said Don Close, livestock analyst with PHI Marketing.
"Packers may ease back a little Tuesday and Wednesday and push higher for some numbers Thursday and Friday," Close said.
Slipping pork prices also could lend weakness, Close said.
Fresh pork prices at midday were quoted lower, with hams off $1.00-$2.00 per cwt, pork bellies down $3.00, but trimmings up $1.00-$2.00, USDA said in its central U.S. carlot report.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs at plant were seen at $59.50 to $60.00 per cwt on Tuesday, and Illinois top prices were expected at $59.50-$60.00, sources in those areas said.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs at plants were seen at $60.00-$60.50, sources there said.
